The Emperor did not ask the German command to take over the Italian front in October 1918. What actually happened: the Germans had no reserve to give, and were themselves asking for an armistice by the second week of November. The dependence on Germany that had grown since Gorlice in May 1915, through the Supreme War Command of September 1916 and the German-commanded army at Caporetto, was already complete, and ended with the Central Powers' defeat. The monarchy's armies were never formally put under German command, but each acceptance of a German commander or a German plan, from Mackensen's army in 1915 to the Fourteenth Army in 1917, took something from what the Austro-Hungarian General Staff decided for itself.
